examples.question_text: A square pyramid is $12$ cm high. Two slices parallel to its base are taken at different heights. Sketch the shape of each cross-section. Explain whether the pyramid has a uniform cross-section.

Solid $A$ is a cylinder $9$ cm high. Solid $B$ is a pentagonal prism $7$ cm long. For each solid, name the cross-section parallel to its end faces. Explain whether it has a uniform cross-section and whether it is a prism.

examples.solution_text:
The slice extends along the prism's length. Its four sides meet at right angles, so the cross-section is a rectangle.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[draw=black]
\draw (0,0) rectangle (3,1.5);
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
This slicing plane is not parallel to the triangular bases. Higher horizontal slices are narrower rectangles. Slices parallel to the triangular bases remain identical triangles, so the solid is still a prism.

examples.question_text: A cone has base diameter $8$ cm. A vertical slicing plane passes through its apex and the centre of its base. Sketch and name the cross-section. How does it differ from a slice parallel to the base?
examples.solution_text:
The vertical plane cuts the base along a diameter and meets the apex, giving a triangle.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[draw=black]
\draw (0,0)--(3,0)--(1.5,3)--cycle;
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
A slice parallel to the base is a circle. These circles shrink towards the apex, so the cone does not have a uniform cross-section.

examples.derivation: The section lies at constant depth halfway between the triangular ends. Its vertices are a translation of the end triangle, so it is an identical triangle.

Sections parallel to a square pyramid's base are squares whose side lengths decrease towards the apex. Different sizes establish that the cross-section is not uniform. The sketches illustrate this without claiming specified slice heights.

Parallel end-face sections of the cylinder are identical circles; those of the pentagonal prism are identical pentagons. Both are uniform, but only the polygonal solid with rectangular lateral faces is a prism under the supplied definition.

The triangular ends occupy parallel planes perpendicular to the extrusion direction. Their stated perpendicular separation is 8 cm, so h=8 cm along the length. Sections parallel to these bases are identical triangles. The dimension arrow follows the projected extrusion direction.

At vertical coordinate 1, the triangular profile intersects at horizontal coordinates 0.75 and 2.25. Extruding this segment through depth 0 to 3 produces a rectangle. Its projected vertices match the red outline. Higher slices narrow; sections parallel to the triangular ends remain identical triangles.

An axial plane intersects the cone's base in a diameter and its curved surface in two straight generators meeting at the apex, forming a triangle. Sections parallel to the base are circles that decrease in size towards the apex.
